newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- DEC 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- DEC 5.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The government fears a widening of protests as the farmers' blockade of road and rail communication enters its eighth day and port employees threaten to paralyse the main port of Piraeus. Teachers and students open another front, declaring strikes and occupations.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis has sent a letter to Greece's European Union partners ahead of next week's summit in Dublin stressing the need for solidarity and territorial integrity and noting that Greece's recently announced arms programme would make it difficult for the country to achieve convergence targets.
--The government yesterday submitted to Parliament its new tax bill cutting back on hundreds of tax breaks and imposing new taxes on real estate holdings.
--Health Minister Costas Geitonas yesterday announced plans to merge various health services into a network of primary care centres in large towns and cities.

--Simitis asks Greece's European Union partners for 'solidarity and sensitivity' in the event Greece misses Maastricht targets because of the massive armaments programme Turkey's provocations has forced it to accept.

--Students take to the streets of Larissa to support the farmers as Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas fails to make any headway. The word now falls to Simitis. Meanwhile, there appears to be dissension in the ranks of the unionist movement between pro-government and opposition-aligned factions over strategy.
--New evidence has led to the release of a woman imprisoned for murder. Police now say that a gang carried out a series of murders.

--The recently-published biography of Queen Sophia of Spain - a member of the former Greek royal family - claims that the dynasty wanted only the best for Greece and were thwarted by foreigners, the military and former president Constantine Karamanlis.
--The Greek Orthodox Church will also be liable for the government's new real estate tax, reports state, following the government's submission of the new bill to Parliament.
--Simitis calls on all to bear the burden in a dramatic appeal to the people, warning of Greece's collapse if the budget is not adhered to.
--In muddy Xanthi, hard hit by the weekend's freak storms, bread and blankets are being distributed by military helicopters in border villages now concerned about disease and snowfall.

--US State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns says that the US believes that Greek national air space limits should be the equivalent of its territorial waters. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
